{{Short description|Theorem in algebraic geometry}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Abhyankar–Moh theorem''' states that if <math>L</math> is a [[complex line]] in the complex [[affine plane]] <math>\mathbb{C}^2</math>, then every embedding of <math>L</math> into <math>\mathbb{C}^2</math> extends to an [[automorphism]] of the plane. It is named after [[Shreeram Shankar Abhyankar]] and [[:zh:莫宗坚|Tzuong-Tsieng Moh]], who published it in 1975. More generally, the same theorem applies to lines and planes over any [[algebraically closed field]] of [[Characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] zero, and to certain well-behaved subsets of higher-dimensional complex affine spaces.
